title: Indore Clinic Launches Madhya Pradesh's First Alzheimer's Blood Biomarker Test
excerpt: Sampurna Sodani Diagnostic Clinic in Indore says its new pTau217 and Aβ42 blood test can flag Alzheimer's-related brain changes 10 to 15 years before symptoms, offering a less invasive alternative to spinal taps and PET scans.
body:
• Sampurna Sodani Diagnostic Clinic in Indore has introduced a blood biomarker test for early detection of Alzheimer's disease, the first such service in Madhya Pradesh, according to the clinic.
  • The test evaluates two biomarkers — pTau217 and Aβ42 — and the clinic says it can identify Alzheimer's-related brain changes 10 to 15 years before clinical symptoms appear.
  • The clinic positions the test as a less invasive, more affordable alternative to cerebrospinal fluid tests and Amyloid PET scans, which are not currently available in Indore.
  • Researchers internationally have reported blood-based pTau217 tests achieving high accuracy in identifying Alzheimer's pathology, though experts stress such tests are screening tools, not standalone diagnoses.

In a first for Madhya Pradesh, a diagnostic clinic in Indore has launched a blood biomarker test aimed at detecting Alzheimer's disease up to 10 to 15 years before symptoms such as memory loss appear. Sampurna Sodani Diagnostic Clinic introduced the Blood Biomarker Test for early Alzheimer's detection this week, framing it as a major step for preventive healthcare in central India.

The automated test evaluates two clinically significant biomarkers — pTau217 (phosphorylated tau 217) and Aβ42 (amyloid-beta 42) — both core indicators of Alzheimer's pathology. Elevated levels of these proteins in the blood can signal the amyloid plaque and tau buildup in the brain that characterize the disease, well before cognitive decline becomes visible.

"This new blood-based test is a game-changer for the public. It replaces painful and inaccessible procedures with a simple, highly accurate, and minimally invasive alternative right here in Indore," a spokesperson for Sampurna Healthcare said. "Early diagnosis empowers patients and families to make informed medical decisions, start treatments when they are most effective, and plan for the future with clarity." The clinic recommends the test for individuals aged 50 and above and for people experiencing early memory-related concerns or cognitive decline.

Context & Background

Alzheimer's disease is the leading cause of dementia worldwide, and it is typically diagnosed only after cognitive decline has already severely affected a patient's life. Confirming Alzheimer's pathology has traditionally required either a cerebrospinal fluid test — an invasive lumbar puncture (spinal tap) — or an Amyloid PET scan. Both are costly and difficult to access, and Amyloid PET scan facilities for Alzheimer's are currently not available in Indore, forcing families to travel to distant metropolitan cities, the clinic noted.

The science behind the approach is well established internationally. Swedish neuroscientists developed a pTau217 blood assay — ALZpath — that in three independent clinical studies of 786 patients showed high diagnostic accuracy in identifying amyloid plaques, with reported accuracy of about 96% for elevated beta-amyloid and up to 97% for tau, according to research published in JAMA Neurology. A study published in April 2026 in Nature Communications by Mass General Brigham investigators found that plasma pTau217 could detect changes consistent with early Alzheimer's progression before amyloid PET scans showed anything abnormal. Lead author Dr. Hyun-Sik Yang called it "a fundamental shift in the timeline of Alzheimer's detection."

Still, experts urge measured expectations. A 2026 study found that elevated pTau217 does not guarantee symptoms — they may appear within a year, within 15 years, or not at all. Researchers emphasize that current blood-biomarker models are screening tools that complement, not replace, clinical diagnosis, cognitive testing and brain imaging.

Impact & Analysis

For families in Madhya Pradesh, the practical shift is access: a blood draw at a local diagnostic clinic instead of a spinal tap or a trip to a metro for a PET scan. If the test performs as advertised, it gives at-risk patients a long planning window — lifestyle adjustments, closer medical monitoring, eligibility for clinical trials and, as new amyloid-targeting treatments emerge, therapy at the stage when it is most effective.

The broader significance is timing. India is aging, and dementia care remains expensive and concentrated in a handful of cities. Bringing biomarker screening into tier-2 cities like Indore is the kind of decentralization that could matter at scale — provided the testing is paired with proper counseling, confirmatory pathways and honest communication about what a positive biomarker result does and does not mean.

"Early diagnosis empowers patients and families to make informed medical decisions, start treatments when they are most effective, and plan for the future with clarity."

— Spokesperson, Sampurna Healthcare

Diaspora Angle

For diaspora families with aging parents in India, the test adds a concrete option for elder-care planning back home: a blood-based screening in a tier-2 city can give NRIs coordinating care from abroad an earlier, clearer picture of a parent's cognitive health without requiring travel to a metro hospital.

What's Next

The test is now available through the clinic in Indore, with the 50-plus and memory-concern populations as the primary audience. Watch for whether other diagnostic chains in central India follow suit — and for how neurologists integrate blood biomarkers into routine practice, including which patients get counseled toward confirmatory testing after a positive screen.
